subject: Architecture
title: Mud Brick: The First Building Material
description: A quick, practical guide to Mud Brick: The First Building Material.

hook.text: The oldest known bricks are 11,000 years old, found in the Jordan Valley.

buildup.text: Early builders mixed mud with straw and dried it in the sun. No kiln needed.

discovery.text: Mud brick let humans build permanent walls, rooms, and multi-story structures.

twist.text: The material is still used today. A third of the world's population lives in earthen buildings.

climax.text: Adobe, cob, and rammed earth are all variations of the same ancient idea.

punchline.text: Dirt and water built civilizations. They still do.

quiz.question: What fraction of the world's population lives in earthen buildings?
